top_signals.title: The Anti-Taliban Resistance Has Survived. Can It Win?
top_signals.summary:
As the Taliban enters its sixth year in power, it remains more powerful than it was before the Sept. 11 attacks. The Taliban’s flag flies in all of Afghanistan’s 34 provinces. While only Russia has formally recognized the group as the country’s government, China and the United Arab Emirates have officially accredited or accepted Taliban ambassadors and exchanged diplomatic staff, with Pakistan, Qatar, Iran, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, and Turkey establishing de facto working relationships with the Sunni Deobandi group. top_signals.title: US Army practices digging temporary battlefield graves
top_signals.summary: The Army is preparing for the grim possibility of burying fallen soldiers on the battlefield, testing how fast it can dig temporary graves while preserving remains for eventual identification and return to families after the end of a conflict.

top_signals.title: Mexico truckers reach deal for talks after strike disrupts 19 states
top_signals.summary:
Trucking organizations in Mexico have agreed to four negotiating sessions with federal officials after a nationwide strike disrupted highways and threatened freight movements across the country.
